commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot Duke -> Jaku, add greeting and exit
commitResults.messageBody:
Level-0 requires the chatbot to have its own name, so that it is
distinguishable from the placeholder Duke used by the template, and to
greet the user and exit instead of only printing a banner.

Rename Duke.java to Jaku.java (the file name must match the public
class name) and replace the Duke ASCII art with a JAKU banner, so that
no trace of the placeholder name remains. The greeting and farewell are
extracted into greet() and exit() methods rather than being inlined in
main(), keeping each method at a single level of abstraction as the
chatbot grows.

Update the two documentation references that the rename made stale: the
setup step in README.md, which pointed at the old file and class name,
and the user guide title in docs/README.md. Also fill in the student
profile in AGENTS.md, so that AI tools reading it have accurate context.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add echo loop, exit on bye command
commitResults.messageBody:
Level-1 requires the chatbot to respond to the user rather than exiting
immediately, so that later increments have a conversation loop to build
commands into.

Read input line by line with a Scanner and echo each line back until the
user enters bye. The loop guards on hasNextLine() so that reaching the
end of the input, for example when input is piped in or the user presses
Ctrl-D, ends the conversation cleanly instead of throwing
NoSuchElementException. The bye command is trimmed and matched
case-insensitively, so stray whitespace or capitals still exit as the
user intended, and blank lines are skipped so that pressing Enter alone
does not print an empty reply.

Move the command word into a BYE_COMMAND constant alongside the existing
constants, and give the greeting and farewell a warmer tone now that the
user actually converses with Jaku.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for storing and listing items
commitResults.messageBody:
Level-2 requires Jaku to remember what the user enters and show it back on
request, instead of echoing each line and forgetting it.

Store the items in an ArrayList held behind the List interface. The course
allows a fixed String[100], but a list avoids both the arbitrary cap and a
separate count field that has to be kept in step with the contents. The
element type will become a task object in a later increment, and that change
stays confined to this field and the methods that touch it.

Turn Jaku into an instance rather than a set of static methods, so the item
list is an ordinary field instead of static mutable state. main() now just
delegates to run(), which reads as a summary of the whole session.

Route each line through handleCommand(), which shows the list for the list
command and otherwise treats the line as a new item, as Level-2 specifies.
Proper command parsing and unknown-command errors belong to later
increments. Generalise the old echo() into two reply() overloads, since
listing needs to print several lines inside one pair of dividers, and answer
with a short message when the list is empty rather than printing an empty
block that would look broken.
Represent each task with a Task object so its description and completion state stay together. Support marking and unmarking tasks and show their status in task listings.
Keep exact console expectations in a shared test plan and run them through a project-local skill so behavior regressions are detected after Java changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add typed todo deadline and event tasks
commitResults.messageBody: Parse the three Level 4 task commands and preserve their date and time text so users can distinguish each task type in confirmations and listings.
Model todos, deadlines, and events as Task subclasses so shared completion behavior stays in the base class while each subtype owns its display details.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle empty todos and unknown commands
commitResults.messageBody: Route expected command mistakes through a checked JakuException so invalid input receives a framed reply without terminating the chat session.
Validate timed-task syntax and task indexes before accessing data so every expected input mistake receives actionable guidance without changing task state.
Remove tasks from the existing collection by their validated list number and report both the removed task and the updated task count.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use an enum for chatbot commands
commitResults.messageBody: Represent supported commands as enum values and dispatch them with a switch so command recognition and argument extraction share one type-safe model.
Save the task list after each successful mutation and restore it from an OS-independent relative path when Jaku starts.
Use isolated data fixtures to verify save and load behavior, corrupted-record recovery, and that failed writes leave Jaku's task list unchanged.
Keep task data durable across Jaku sessions while preserving the required branch-and-merge workflow for this increment.

Deadlines previously preserved arbitrary due-date text. This made
date-aware behavior impossible and saved non-date values inconsistent.

Parse ISO dates into LocalDate and format them for display.
Save the canonical ISO form so startup can validate saved records.

Treat non-ISO legacy deadline records as malformed. This preserves the
existing silent-skip policy.

Deadlines now use validated ISO calendar dates rather than arbitrary
text.

Merge the verified Level 8 work so users receive consistent date display
and persistence.

commitResults.messageTitle: refactor: separate Jaku UI parsing and task storage
refactor: organize Jaku classes into packages
build: configure Gradle to run Jaku
test: add JUnit coverage for parsing and task indexing

commitResults.messageBody:
Jaku coordinates the lifecycle of a chat session, but that responsibility was not stated in its class documentation.

Document the load, command-processing, and delegation lifecycle so callers can understand the coordinator's role without reading its implementation.

Make Parser explicitly non-instantiable because it provides only static parsing utilities.

Storage contains two serialization statements longer than the Java coding standard's 120-character hard limit.\n\nWrap those expressions at argument boundaries to improve readability while preserving the existing persistence format and behavior.

Users cannot search the task list by keyword, making it harder to locate tasks in a longer list.

Add a case-insensitive find command that returns matching task descriptions in their existing order. Show clear guidance for a missing keyword and a normal reply when no tasks match.

Keep search read-only so it does not affect saved task data.
